final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative hydrophobic swap in the globular head with neutral PLM score, best ProteinMPNN delta (+1.89), and Leu observed in ~11% of homologs, indicating good viability with potential to tune the receptor/F-interaction surface. Phenotype gain remains inferred, not measured.

Highly conservative acidic substitution with neutral PLM score, favorable structural compatibility, and MSA precedent, giving very low viability risk near a surface loop potentially relevant to receptor engagement. Expected entry-efficiency gain is modest.

Well-supported by PLM (0.86) and MSA (Ala observed in homologs), removing the Thr hydroxyl could subtly alter the 303-306 surface loop relevant to receptor binding while preserving fold. Phenotype benefit is speculative but structurally plausible.

stop_reason.detail: All applicable evidence dimensions are exhausted and further calls (static annotation, safety toxin screen) are unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: Position 411 sits in an N-X-T glycosylation sequon (N411-N412-T413); removing a head-domain glycan shield can increase receptor access and F-triggering, potentially raising entry efficiency.
Located in the C-terminal receptor-binding head near the ephrin-B2/B3 interface; a conservative Asn-to-Gln change may tune receptor contacts without disrupting the fold.
Lowest PLM (0.32) and zero mutant frequency with mediocre coverage; demoted from rank 1 — initial rationale now weakly supported.
E509 lies in the C-terminal receptor-binding head near conserved ephrin-interaction residues; a conservative charge-neutralizing change may tune receptor affinity/F-triggering balance.
Surface-exposed residue in the receptor-binding domain; charge-softening substitution could improve receptor engagement while remaining structurally conservative.
PLM and structure acceptable, but MSA applicability is very low (7/21 homologs, Q never observed) — demoted below better-supported candidates.
T303 is in the globular head distal to disulfides; small side-chain reduction could relax local packing and modulate conformational transitions needed for F activation.
Small conservative change in the stalk-head connecting region that may modulate F-triggering conformational dynamics.
Good PLM (0.86) and MSA support (A seen in homologs, app 0.95); removing the Thr OH could subtly alter local surface near the 303-306 loop relevant to receptor engagement.
F396 is a bulky aromatic in the head domain; conservative hydrophobic swap (F->L) may alter receptor-induced conformational signaling while preserving fold.
Conservative hydrophobic swap in the head domain; plausibly tolerated and could subtly alter receptor-binding surface.

Strongest overall: PLM-neutral (1.0), best ProteinMPNN ΔlogP (+1.89), and Leu observed in 11% of homologs — conservative hydrophobic swap in the globular head, likely to preserve fold while potentially tuning receptor/F-interaction surface.
Y337 aromatic-to-aromatic substitution removes a hydroxyl while keeping the aromatic ring, a low-risk probe of local interaction networks in the head domain.
Minimal aromatic substitution (loss of hydroxyl) in the head region; likely tolerated, may affect local H-bonding relevant to conformational triggering.
High PLM (0.94) and decent structure score; F absent in homologs but the position is variable (entropy 2.0), so evolution signal is weak rather than damaging.
Highly conservative acidic-sidechain shortening near the head-domain surface; minimal structural risk while subtly changing local electrostatics.
Very conservative acidic substitution near the stalk-head boundary; low risk but uncertain gain.
PLM-neutral (1.0) and structure-favorable (ΔlogP +0.68); conservative acidic swap with MSA precedent (5%) — very low viability risk.
Conservative basic-residue swap at a surface position; preserves charge and viability, may adjust surface interactions relevant to receptor engagement.
Conservative basic-residue swap; retains charge while altering side-chain geometry in a region implicated in F interaction.
Conservative K→R with MSA precedent and moderate PLM/structure scores; safe but low expected phenotype gain.
Hydrophobic-to-aromatic change in the head domain could strengthen local packing or inter-subunit contacts that influence G-F triggering.
Hydrophobic-to-aromatic change in the head domain; moderate structural risk, kept pending evidence.
Moderate PLM/structure scores but F never observed in homologs; kept as backup only.
